name: agweb
works_with: Claude Code and Codex (agent skill), any agent that can run shell commands
short: A macOS browser your coding agents drive from the shell. It never takes focus, and you can watch every agent's tabs live.
what: agweb is a WebKit browser for coding agents on macOS. Agents control it with an `agweb` command that copies playwright-cli's commands where it can, and each reply says what changed on the page, so the agent rarely needs a second snapshot. A dashboard shows every agent's tabs at once. Idle tabs are suspended, and ads and trackers are blocked with uBlock Origin's lists.
who: People who run several coding agents at once on a Mac and are tired of Chrome windows stealing focus. If you need Chrome DevTools, Chrome extensions or Playwright attaching to the browser, or you are not on macOS 26, skip it.
needs: Xcode 26 or later, only if you build from source
A coding agent that can run shell commands

steps.title: Install the app
steps.text: Download `Agweb.dmg` from the repo's Releases page, drag Agweb to Applications and open it.

steps.title: Add the command and the agent skill
steps.text: In the app, choose Help ▸ Install Command Line Tool, then Help ▸ Install Agent Skill (for Claude Code and Codex). Both link into the app, so they update with it.

steps.title: Open a page in a workspace
steps.text: Each task gets its own workspace. This starts the app if it is not running, takes a snapshot with `[ref=eN]` handles and clicks a button.
steps.code:
agweb -w task open en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WebKit
agweb -w task snapshot
agweb -w task click 'role=button[name="Main menu"]'

try.label: From the README
try.text: Run `agweb -w task open en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WebKit`, then press ⌘D in the app to see the dashboard with every agent's tabs.

watch: It is WebKit only. Playwright and Chrome extensions cannot attach, and Chrome-only sites may misbehave.
A named profile (`-p work`) keeps its logins and is shared by every agent using it at the same time.
It downloads uBlock Origin's filter lists every 4 days. YouTube ads and some ad blocker walls still get through.
`fill --secret-cmd` types a password from a command such as `pass show site` so the agent never sees it in replies.
